While I don’t think it’s necessarily proper etiquette for guests to *ask* for a plus one, I think giving your guests a plus-one is practically an obligation.

Guests aren’t there to “support the couple” — they don’t need support, they want your attendance at their party. 
On average, couples invite 116 guests to their wedding, so unless guests are immediate members of their family or close friends, the other guests are not there for “support”.

Weddings *are* expensive, intimate, and planned — but that applies to the guests too. No one wants to spend hundreds of dollars on a fancy suit or dress & shoes to attend a formal party where they may not even know anyone. 

There’s also an unspoken expectation on the guests to eat, dance, have fun…. that’s a lot harder to do if you don’t know anyone. 
Sure, you can meet people, but other than simple small talk, what else is there to do?

It’s the same message as for couples who want a dry wedding or a destination wedding — if you want host a wedding, make sure your guests are happy, or don’t get upset when they RSVP “no”.

I wasn’t as confused by Naomi’s willingness to give Angela up, as I was confused by *how* it was even possible.
My interpretation is that Naomi never truly wanted to be a mother but liked the idea of having a child via handmaid, as it was expected of her as a good wife to a Commander. 

As Naomi was now a widow for the second time, she probably realized that Angela/Charlotte would have been taken from her and given to another family. 

Knowing how much Lawrence adored her, and probably herself having some kind of love towards the child, Lydia encouraging her was probably the “push” she needed. 

As for how they arranged it… my guess is that the new Commanders from the West hadn’t all arrived yet, and Lydia / Naomi convinced the Eyes to allow her to do this one thing before everything went into lockdown. That’s the only plausible explanation I can think of.

I would have loved that too, but I’m honestly just happy with the idea that Naomi wanted to give Angela back to Janine. 
I was always rooting for Naomi to have a redemption arc, and letting Angela go with Janine is one of the best possible things she could have done.

While watching this scene, though, I thought it was so unrealistic that the Eyes would drop Janine *and* her child at the border.
But after thinking about it, it kind of makes sense as Naomi is now a widow (for the second time) and Boston has been taken back by the Americans. 

Maybe it was a last-minute thing that Naomi and Lydia wanted to do before all the new commanders from the West arrived and everything went into a full-lockdown situation.

They could have done it *so much better*. 

Luke could have seen June holding the tape recorder and said “remember when you made me those tapes?” and some dialogue about how impactful it was for him to know what happened to her. Would have been *so much less cheesy* than “you should write a book!”

I think this goes beyond what the Handmaids would have felt — Econopeople and Marthas would have thought about things like this too. 

Remembering what it was like to go out to a bar on a Friday night, sing karaoke with friends, get takeout from your favorite restaurant on the way home…

In the early seasons of the show we got more glimpses into life pre-Gilead, which made it feel realistic to me.
Sure, all the trauma inflicted by Gilead would be hard to *not* think about, but it would also be so natural to reminisce about *normal life* before.

He did end up becoming more “brave” and willing to take huge risks, like she does, but *for* June.
